A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EG-XC research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–O are readable and complete. The additional bibliography page in v3 does not limit comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original EG-XC experiments on MD17, 3BPA, and QM9, alongside ablations, additional appendix comparisons, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The density embeddings, equivariant message passing, two readouts, and differentiable SCF training are unchanged. Section 4 adds attribution without changing the algorithm or its equations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MD17, 3BPA, QM9, and cumulene-chain runtime evaluations, with identical interpolation, structural extrapolation, molecular-size extrapolation, and supplementary test coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated force fields, delta-learning variants, XC functionals, and appendix comparators are unchanged. The newly cited Remme and Gasteiger works are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5, Table 4, and the appendices retain the same splits, sample sizes, energy-only training, metrics, model settings, and SCF evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The component ablation in Table 3, reduced-data MD17 tests, alternative delta-learning comparisons, potential-energy surfaces, runtime analyses, and physical-constraint study are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Appendix N still reports the minimum of ten runtime repetitions, and neither version adds confidence intervals or uncertainty estimates for prediction errors.

E6.justification: All experimental tables and figures retain their values and findings. For example, EG-XC's aspirin MAE remains 0.69 mEh in Table 1, and its 3BPA 1200K relative MAE remains 1.39 mEh in Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–50, appendix derivations, and runtime complexity analysis are unchanged. The added citations introduce no new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions and claims about non-local modeling, energy-only training, accuracy, data efficiency, and extrapolation.

C2.justification: The explanations of generalization and physical constraints remain unchanged, as do limitations concerning nuclear-position dependence, systems without nuclei, spin information, and computational cost.

D1.justification: Near Equation 14, v3 identifies Gasteiger et al. (2022) as the source of the fixed polynomial envelope, replacing an unresolved citation. This clarifies an implementation source; the formula, hyperparameters, implementation procedures, hardware information, and code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Remme et al. (2023), KineticNet, to Section 3 and explicitly acknowledges a similar density-convolution embedding in Section 4. It also adds Gasteiger et al. (2022) to resolve two missing filter references. These are localized attribution and positioning improvements.

P1.justification: Sections 3–4 receive localized citation edits and a rewritten embedding-description sentence. Several bibliography metadata entries are edited, while section organization and the broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Citation additions cause limited text reflow and move the final bibliography entry onto a mostly empty additional page, shifting the appendices by one page. All seven figures and nine tables retain their content, captions, and designs.

improvement.justification: v3 improves attribution by acknowledging Remme et al.'s related embedding and replacing two unresolved citations with Gasteiger et al. (2022), including the source of the polynomial envelope. These corrections improve scholarly context and technical traceability; the scientific method, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
